title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary; the preregistered harmful-change mapping and the per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and we give the exact reproducibility path in Methods. We report results strictly according to the preregistration and archived execution artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in program repair and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) reports that inserting deterministic verifiers between generation and acceptance can raise verifier-detected pass rates while revealing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps show that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is limited. A central methodological concern is intervention informativeness: verifier-guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We therefore ran a preregistered controlled-fault injection (deterministic, outcome-independent) with shared controlled-fault pairing to ensure the intervention could be meaningfully exercised. Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Empirical evaluations of verifier-interposed repair show repeatable gains in verifier-detected pass rates in program-repair and IaC settings where compact mechanical predicates exist [1]. Work evaluating verifier-first or verifier-guided strategies for IaC and code demonstrates practical improvements but also documents new failure modes tied to verifier coverage and optimization dynamics [2]. Controlled analyses have highlighted verifier-exploitation risk in iterative refinement designs and recommend mitigation strategies such as multi-verifier ensembles or constrained repair budgets [3]. Other recent studies emphasize a measurable "verifier tax" (added interaction steps, compute, and latency) that impacts operational cost–latency tradeoffs for verifier-mediated agent pipelines [4]. Surveys and NetOps-focused overviews caution that gains in read-oriented assistance do not automatically transfer to safe closed-loop configuration changes without conservative orchestration and strong verification [5].

(Each numeric citation above maps to the verified bibliographic record listed in References and the archived evidence bundle; the cited records were used to support the specific empirical or methodological claims just summarized.)
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The binary success predicate requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and simulator-based compliance agreement (verifier+simulator).

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each task pair had exactly one sampled initial generation reused by both arms and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The execution manifest records planned task_count = 40, completed_episode_count = 78, complete_pair_count = 39, model_calls_used = 118, and controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6.

Model sampling and per-call records. The archived model configuration declares requested model = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; differences in outcomes therefore stem from the presence/absence of exposed diagnostics under the preregistered repair budget. Per-call runtime sampling parameters, hosted-provider traces, and per-call metadata required to inspect sampling behavior are archived in the evidence bundle: see execution/model_configuration.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json (locations recorded in the execution manifest) for the full per-call sampling records and provider traces.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure meaningful intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (examples: dropped-required-restore, protected-interface change, make-before-break uplink switchover). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; the run produced source_generation_attempt_count = 40 with source_valid_count = 39 and source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1, producing one excluded pair documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring and the preregistered harmful-change mapping. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator agreement. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling schema used for the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis; the executable transformation implementing that mapping is archived in execution/transformation_manifest.json. Compact operational mapping used by the archived scoring pipeline (and documented here as required for reproducibility): label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The archived per-episode validator traces include violation_codes and are available at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl for independent aggregation.

Statistical analysis. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired-binomial). We report discordant-pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, a two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' exclusion; a sensitivity analysis treats missing episodes as failures. Multiplicity: single predefined primary test; subgroup/per-fault-class analyses labeled exploratory.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs), failed_episode_count = 2, model_calls_used = 118 (<=120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Start and completion UTC timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success (blind repair) = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success (verifier-guided) = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). The archived analysis artifacts analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv record these outputs and their hashes are present in the evidence manifest.

Missingness and exclusions. One preregistered exclusion occurred: a source-generation attempt was invalid and produced two unscorable episodes (both_missing_pairs = 1). The 'complete_pair_primary' rule excluded that pair from the primary analysis; terminal error records and per-episode logs are archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration defined a confirmatory harmful-overrepair test (threshold <= 5% absolute increase). The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because that preregistered aggregation is absent from the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a confirmatory safety verdict here. To reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic deterministically from the archive, auditors must: iterate the complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows complete_pairs = 39), for each pair read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), apply the compact harmful-change mapping (harmful if violation_codes includes PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE), compute paired counts of harmful indicators (guarded vs baseline), and run the preregistered paired test per the analysis plan. All required per-episode fields and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/execution_manifest.json). Any harmful-overrepair summary produced outside the archived confirmatory executor is exploratory unless recomputed and added to the archive following the preregistered pipeline.

Representative diagnostics. Example per-pair scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json). Illustrative cases show guarded repairs using validator diagnostics to avoid protected-interface edits and to restore required command sequences that blind repair sometimes omitted; these per-episode traces are archived for inspection.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-controlled-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated success on the tested synthetic fault bank. The paired shared-candidate design isolates the effect of diagnostic exposure because both arms received the same initial faulty candidate and identical repair budgets; only diagnostic exposure differed.

Mechanism. Archived validator_trace.violation_codes and per-episode scoring traces illustrate targeted corrective edits: diagnostics often pinpointed a protected field or an omitted restore step and guided the guarded repair to include the missing commands or to avoid protected-interface modifications. These traces provide a plausible causal pathway from explicit diagnostics to improved post-repair verifier outcomes without changing the initial sampled candidate.

Safety boundary and open confirmatory safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis remains unresolved in the archived confirmatory summary because the aggregator was not computed by the archived analysis executor. We therefore do not claim a confirmatory safety verdict here. The preregistered harmful-change mapping and the per-episode traces needed for deterministic reproduction are archived and their exact artifact locations are documented above, enabling independent recomputation and audit.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Execution accounting shows a measurable interaction budget (hosted-model calls = 118; stage_counts recorded in the provider_call_audit). Practitioners should weigh verifier-mediated accuracy gains against increased call counts, latency, and cost. Verifier coverage is a practical limiter: diagnostics cannot correct what the verifier cannot detect, and narrow verifiers risk encouraging optimization to the detectable surface. Ensembles of verifiers or explicit harmful-change constraints are practical mitigations.

Threats to validity. Internal: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and the exactly-one initial generation per pair constrain claims about generation determinism; pairing semantics ensure observed arm differences are due to diagnostics under the adapter contract. Construct: primary success depended on verifier+simulator agreement; their coverage and fidelity bound operational meaning of "valid". External: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic, template-based controlled-fault bank limit generalization to heterogeneous vendor devices and naturalistic task streams. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed primary contrast but limited power for per-fault-class subgroup inference. Future replications should expand model families, verifier ensembles, and task distributions.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769, 0.359]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved; however, the transformation implementing the harmful-change mapping and all per-episode traces required for deterministic recomputation are archived and their locations are documented above, enabling independent adjudication. We release the full artifact bundle to facilitate reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies before operational deployment.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (see execution/transformation_manifest.json and the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
